# Why Disclosure Fails

The problem is not a lack of information, but a lack of attention. Investors receive more
disclosure every year, and they read less of it. The average 10-K now runs past eighty thousand
words. Disclosure isn't a remedy; it's a ritual.

Regulators keep adding mandates. Each mandate answers a scandal, and each one lengthens the filing.
None of them is ever repealed. More disclosure does not mean more transparency; it means more noise.

This is not just a regulatory problem -- it is a cultural one. Firms write for lawyers, and lawyers
write for courts. In the end, what gets disclosed is not what matters, and what matters is not
disclosed.
